subject.title: [Feature] Queue prompts when API limits prevent an immediate response

question: Should OpenClaw add a core SQLite-backed capacity-wait queue for prompts blocked by provider/model API limits, and how should it coordinate with the existing open queue/cooldown PRs?
rationale: The remaining work is not a narrow bug patch: it changes persistent runtime state, provider retry semantics, user-visible wait state, and how partial PRs should be adopted or replaced.

options.title: Sponsor durable capacity-wait queue
options.body: Design the queue as core SQLite state with replay/visibility semantics, then land or replace related PR slices only where they fit that design.

options.title: Narrow to followup restart persistence
options.body: Treat provider-limit auto-replay as separate future work and only pursue durable followup queues across restart first.

options.title: Keep current failover behavior
options.body: Accept cooldown copy/session suspension as the intended behavior and close the broader automatic replay direction later with an explicit product decision.

recommendation.title: Sponsor durable capacity-wait queue
recommendation.body: Design the queue as core SQLite state with replay/visibility semantics, then land or replace related PR slices only where they fit that design.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows broad queue and model-fallback ownership signals, making this the best available routing candidate for the cross-cutting product choice.
